Topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D Intuition

Target audience: University students (STEM majors) or curious lifelong learners

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Intuition: Expanding Dimensions

Lecture lines:
Dimensions define how we measure space and volume.
1D: Two points on a line.
2D: A disk in a plane.
3D: A volume in space.
General formula: Sum of x squared equals r squared.

Planned animations:
Fade in central point in 2D space.
Transform point to line, then square.
Highlight center and corners of square.
Compare square volume to inner circle area.
Show growth rate of corners vs center.

Section: section_2 — The Counter-Intuitive Volume Collapse

Lecture lines:
As dimensions increase, volume behaves strangely.
Total volume concentrates near the sphere's surface.
Almost all volume resides in the peel.
The center becomes practically empty.
Counter-intuitive compared to 3D.

Planned animations:
Display 1D unit segment [0, 1].
Show 2D unit square area = 1.
Extend to 3D cube volume = 1.
Animate N-dimensions unit hypercube.
Contrast volume of sphere inside hypercube.

Section: section_3 — The Corner Problem: Cubes vs. Spheres

Lecture lines:
Consider a sphere inside a hypercube.
Sphere volume vanishes relative to the cube.
Corners stretch far from the center.

Planned animations:
Display N-dimensional hypercube in #FFFFFF.
Render inscribed N-sphere in #FF00FF.
Highlight corner volume excess area.

Section: section_4 — Practical Application: High-Dimensional Data

Lecture lines:
Data in high dimensions hides on surfaces.
Curse of dimensionality affects distance metrics.
Distance resembles navigation on a hypersphere.

Planned animations:
Represent data points as dots in high-D.
Highlight sparsity in high-dimensional space.
Contrast nearest-neighbor distance with average distance.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Reflection

Lecture lines:
High-dimensional geometry isn't just theory.
It transforms complex data into structure.
Geometry is a foundational computational tool.

Planned animations:
Recap hypercube volume logic.
Summarize sphere-in-cube ratio trend.
Highlight significance of high-D geometric intuition.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Reflection", [
            "High-dimensional geometry isn't just theory.",
            "It transforms complex data into structure.",
            "Geometry is a foundational computational tool."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        sphere = Sphere(radius=1.0, color=BLUE).set_opacity(0.5)
        # Using a VGroup of small dots to simulate a data cloud
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.random.normal(0, 0.4, 3), color=YELLOW) for _ in range(50)])
        data_cloud = self.place_in_area(dots, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(sphere, data_cloud))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Indicate(self.lecture[2]))
        self.wait(2)
